patch.value: The coverage gate reports one hundred percent while the security scanner it is supposed to guard is not measured at all

The coverage gate in this repository reports coverage-gate: 5 source file(s) reported, thresholds met at 100 percent lines, branches and functions. scripts/shell-command-scan.ts, which is 1663 lines and is the scanner this repository uses to find shell-command constructions, is not one of the five. It is absent from the report entirely rather than present with a low number.

The cause is that coverageGate.sources is an enumerated list. It reads dot, scripts/coverage-gate.ts, scripts/docstring-gate.ts and scripts/verify-release-publish-attestation.ts. The tsconfig include is star dot ts, which matches the package root and does not recurse, so the dot entry contributes the root files only and every script has to be named individually. shell-command-scan.ts was added later and never was. A file that nobody remembers to enumerate is therefore not merely under-measured, it is invisible: the gate cannot report a gap it was never pointed at.

The scanner is not untested. test/shell-command-scan.test.ts exists and passes. What is missing is enforcement, and the difference matters: adding the file to sources and re-running the gate produces 99.04 percent lines and 98.05 percent branches, failing the 100 percent threshold, with sixteen uncovered lines at 1138-1140, 1142-1143, 1151-1152, 1163, 1173-1175, 1360-1361 and 1583-1585. Those lines have been unexercised for as long as the file has existed, in a scanner whose job is to decide whether a publish is attested.

Worth checking rather than assuming for the rest of the fleet: pm-ops declares sources as dot alone and measures thirteen files including every script, so its gate walks subdirectories where this one does not. The two coverage-gate.ts implementations are 438 and 497 lines and have diverged, which is the same vendored-copy drift that the attestation scanner had before it was consolidated into pm-ops. The extent across the other repositories cannot be read off the configuration and has to be measured per repository by comparing the gate's reported file list against the files on disk.

scripts/shell-command-scan.ts is enumerated in coverageGate.sources and the gate enforces the same 100 percent threshold on it as on every other source file; the sixteen uncovered lines are covered by tests that exercise the behaviour reaching them rather than by calling internals directly, and no guard is deleted to reach the number; the gate is shown to fail when the file is removed from sources or when a line in it goes uncovered; and the per-repository measurement for the rest of the fleet is recorded rather than inferred from configuration
